originalTitle: Zuckerberg pushes ‘superintelligent’ AI for all as Meta drops open-source model
summary: Meta CEO presents utopian vision of AI in 6,000-word essay amid Silicon Valley debate over government regulation
content: Mark Zuckerberg published a lengthy essay on Monday detailing his views on artificial intelligence and announced several plans for how Meta would develop the technology in the future. The CEO’s essay went online the same day as Meta released a new, open-source AI model that seeks to rival Anthropic and OpenAI’s products called Muse Glimmer. Over the course of more than 6,000 words in a post titled “The Future is for Everyone,” Zuckerberg addressed a range of topics related to AI that included datacenters, government regulation, cybersecurity, the creation of bioweapons, labor market disruption, surveillance powers and more. The essay presented a utopian vision of AI as a personalized “superintelligence” – using the word 60 times. “Some argue that superintelligence itself or a small set of experts who control it should decide what is best for humanity. We disagree,” Zuckerberg wrote. Central to Zuckerberg’s post was an argument for free-to-download, open-weight AI models – like the kind Meta develops – and a lack of government regulation of artificial intelligence. Zuckerberg’s stance sets him and Meta apart from industry leaders OpenAI and Anthropic, which have argued that open-source AI is dangerous. The two frontier labs have released proprietary AI products and argued that cutting-edge models should remain tightly controlled by the companies that build them. Zuckerberg’s post comes as Silicon Valley is engaged in a heated debate over how to regulate AI development, which has involved the creation of a secret White House framework for testing new models and an ongoing debate over whether to restrict the use of Chinese-made open-source AI. As Anthropic and OpenAI have surged ahead in the AI industry, competitors such as Meta have also grown wary of their dominance and sought to position their open models as alternatives. Zuckerberg framed Meta’s pursuit of open-weight AI as a more democratic version of the technology and one that will create a “balance of power” between users, whether that involves states, companies or individuals. His plans also called for letting users decide what “values” an AI model should have, as opposed to a company encoding it with rigid guardrails and beliefs. “If the power of superintelligence is held by a small number of individuals, businesses, governments, or AI itself, then that will naturally lead to outcomes that are less favorable for everyone else,” Zuckerberg wrote. Tech leaders have made a cottage industry out of releasing broad, vaguely philosophical treatises on artificial intelligence, which tend to double as marketing materials for their own companies and products. Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, OpenAI’s Sam Altman, Palantir’s Alex Karp and the venture capitalist Marc Andreessen have all written long manifestos on the virtues and dangers of the technology. In addition to weighing in on open source models, Zuckerberg also called for accelerating the buildout of AI infrastructure such as datacenters. The massive development of resource-hungry datacenters has become a divisive issue in the US, with rapidly growing public opposition and calls from politicians to issue moratoriums on their construction. Zuckerberg wrote in the essay that Meta would create a fund to invest more in local communities near datacenters, as well as cited an example from Louisiana where some teachers received a $50,000 bonus check as a result of increased sales tax revenue from the company’s infrastructure investment. On government testing of AI models for cybersecurity risks, a tangible concern after rogue models have hacked outside organizations in recent months, Zuckerberg agreed that companies should share “intermediate training checkpoints and technical staff” but provided few details. He broadly warned that regulation would cause China to overtake the US in the AI race, where he claimed it already has an advantage in terms of building infrastructure. “Any policy that slows American model releases – even by a month – could add significant risk to American leadership while letting foreign models race ahead,” Zuckerberg. Many of Zuckerberg’s policy plans in his essay lacked detail or reiterated previous claims about the abundant wealth and prosperity that AI would create, such as touting that everyone would have “invention superpowers” to create new businesses. His version of the future also is inherently tied to Meta products, such as the company’s AI-enabled smart glasses. “Everyone will have an exceptionally capable personal agent that understands you, your goals, and everything you care about,” Zuckerberg said. “You’ll be able to interact with your agent through any device, including your glasses to keep you present in the moment with the people you care about.” On thornier issues such as loss of jobs from AI, autonomous weapons and government surveillance, Zuckerberg mostly brushed them aside. Law enforcement and the military already possess greater intelligence-gathering powers than the average person, Zuckerberg argued, and this would continue with access to AI. Companies may shrink in size due to AI, he conceded, but the technology would create new economic opportunities. “People will have to adapt, and this will be challenging,” Zuckerberg said about labor disruption from new technology. “But the more that everyone has a personal agent that is superintelligent at teaching us new skills and helping us adapt to change, the smoother this will be.”
chineseTitle: Meta 放弃开源模型，扎克伯格为所有人推动“超级智能”AI
chineseSummary: 在硅谷关于政府监管的争论中，Meta 首席执行官在 6000 字的文章中提出了人工智能的乌托邦愿景
chineseContent: 马克·扎克伯格周一发表了一篇长文，详细阐述了他对人工智能的看法，并宣布了 Meta 未来如何开发该技术的几项计划。这位首席执行官的文章上线的同一天，Meta 发布了一个新的开源人工智能模型，该模型旨在与 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的产品 Muse Glimmer 竞争。扎克伯格在一篇题为“未来属于每个人”的帖子中，在超过 6000 字的内容中讨论了一系列与人工智能相关的话题，包括数据中心、政府监管、网络安全、生物武器的制造、劳动力市场的混乱、监控权力等等。这篇文章提出了人工智能作为个性化“超级智能”的乌托邦愿景——使用这个词 60 次。 “有些人认为，超级智能本身或控制它的一小群专家应该决定什么对人类最有利。我们不同意，”扎克伯格写道。扎克伯格帖子的核心是主张免费下载、开放权重的人工智能模型——就像 Meta 开发的那种——以及政府对人工智能缺乏监管。扎克伯格的立场使他和 Meta 与行业领导者 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 区分开来，后者认为开源人工智能是危险的。这两个前沿实验室已经发布了专有的人工智能产品，并认为尖端模型应继续由构建它们的公司严格控制。扎克伯格发表此文之际，硅谷正就如何监管人工智能发展展开激烈辩论，其中包括创建一个用于测试新模型的秘密白宫框架，以及关于是否限制使用中国制造的开源人工智能的持续辩论。随着 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 在人工智能行业的崛起，Meta 等竞争对手也对其主导地位产生了警惕，
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
